summary.headline: Orders and revenue eased slightly and stayed well behind target, though cancellations improved sharply and year-on-year growth remained strong.

points.what: Orders fell 1.5% week on week to 678, a bad move, while revenue fell 3.0% to $51,003.
points.so_what: Both sit close to the 8-week averages of 683 orders and $49,686 revenue, so the week was steady rather than a break in trend.

points.what: Revenue reached 74.9% of the $68,109 weekly target, leaving a gap of $17,106.
points.so_what: Next week's revenue target of $55,460 is lower, but this shortfall still adds to the quarter's deficit.

points.what: Orders grew 48.4% and revenue 68.4% year on year, both assessed as good.
points.so_what: Both remain below the 75% growth the 2026 targets assume, which is why the week still fell short of target.

points.what: Cancellation rate fell 2.1 pp to 11.4%, a good move and the lowest of the last eight weeks.
points.so_what: Each percentage point of cancellations is worth about $575 of revenue, so this partly cushioned the softer week.

points.what: New signups fell 15.0% week on week to 233, flagged as notable, and were down 3.7% year on year.
points.so_what: Signups are shrinking while orders grow 48.4% year on year, so order growth is not coming from new accounts.

points.what: The cancellation rate move of -2.1 pp is flagged as notable, above the 1.0 pp threshold.
points.so_what: At about $575 of revenue per percentage point, a shift of this size is large enough to matter for weekly revenue.

points.what: The 14-Day Return Rate is reported for the mature week of 29 Dec 2025, as the two most recent weeks are not yet mature.
points.so_what: Return behaviour for the reporting week cannot be read yet, so returns should be judged only on the 29 Dec 2025 week.

points.what: Orders reached 75.3% of the 900 weekly target, 222 behind, and revenue 74.9% of target, $17,106 behind; both are behind.
points.so_what: Next week's targets step down to 828 orders and $55,460 revenue, a lower bar than this week's.

points.what: Quarter-to-date revenue of $150,921 is 83.7% of the $180,401 target to date, a gap of $29,480.
points.so_what: With 10 weeks left, $623,634 is still needed to reach the full-quarter target of $774,555.

points.what: Year-to-date revenue is 83.7% of target, and the $3,888,802 full-year target needs $74,758 a week across the remaining 50 weeks.
points.so_what: The recent 8-week run-rate of $50,363 is well below that required weekly pace.

points.what: EMEA was the biggest driver of the order decline, down 15.4% to 115 orders, a contribution of -21 and 210% of the total change.
points.so_what: EMEA alone more than accounts for the 10-order weekly decline, with other regions offsetting part of it.

points.what: APAC rose 4.7% to 309 orders, contributing +14, LATAM added 1 order, and North America fell 4 to 152.
points.so_what: APAC holds a 45.6% share of orders and offset most of the EMEA weakness this week.

points.what: Search fell 4.0% to 481 orders, contributing -20, while Email rose 29.6% to 35 orders, contributing +8.
points.so_what: Search carries 70.9% of orders, so its direction sets the direction of the weekly total.

points.what: AOV fell 4.0% week on week to $84.86, assessed as bad, but was 5.4% above last year.
points.so_what: Revenue fell 3.0% on a 1.5% order decline, so the lower AOV explains the wider revenue drop.

points.what: The cancellation rate fell 2.1 pp to 11.4% and is 6.3 pp below last year, both good.
points.so_what: At about $575 of revenue per percentage point, the year-on-year improvement is worth meaningful revenue at this week's volume.

points.what: The 14-Day Return Rate for the mature week of 29 Dec 2025 was 11.2%, down 0.2 pp week on week but 1.0 pp above last year, which is bad.
points.so_what: Returns are steady week to week but running above the prior-year level for that week.

points.what: New signups fell 15.0% to 233 and were 3.7% below last year, both bad.
points.so_what: The customer base is not expanding in line with the 48.4% year-on-year growth in orders.

checks.name: 14-Day Return Rate names its mature week
anomaly flag acknowledged in the summary
sentences at most 30 words and 4 numbers
each slot only covers its allowed KPIs
